verdict.rationale: Google's docs say signing in to a Google Account syncs Authenticator codes, and that signing in on a new device restores them automatically. This protects users from lockout when they change devices, which is a documented recovery path that does not need the old phone. Community complaints about wiped tokens and backup exclusion mostly concern device backups and older versions, so they do not concretely contradict cloud sync. Missing for 10: independent hands-on confirmation that sync restores codes after a phone is lost; the sync is opt-in and tied to a Google Account (the app can be used without one); and the QR export path requires the old device, so it offers no documented offline backup for a lost phone.

support.subject: As an everyday user, losing my phone doesn't lose my accounts — a documented recovery path restores my tokens on a new device

citations.quote: When you sign in to your Google Account within Google Authenticator on a new device, your codes are automatically synced to this device.
With Google Authenticator, you can synchronize your verification codes across all your devices, simply by signing in to your Google Account.
This helps protect you from being locked out of your account when you change devices.
